items.description: ANS-184.1: "In a type error, have `arch-validate` print the source scalar and its line next to the parsed value, e.g. `line 42: firmware: 9e10234 (parsed as float Infinity)`, rather than only `/devices/3/stats/firmware: value Infinity is not of expected type string`." At planning the script printed only path, message, schema and hint (Architecture `.claude/architecture/arch-validate.py:100-105`). The service built the type message from the parsed value alone (`service/src/error-translate.ts:188-195`) and parsed with js-yaml, keeping no positions (`service/src/validate.ts:154`).

items.area: R1 — source lines on every error
items.description: Every error in the `POST /api/validate` response that maps to a node of the submitted text carries that node's line, and `arch-validate` prints it. The relation-triple errors (`service/src/validate.ts:194-202`) are included. What the validator accepts or rejects is unchanged. An error with no line keeps today's shape, and the script prints it as before.

The two copies of `arch-validate` stay byte-identical. ArgoCDTools' `aac-tools/image/arch-validate.py` is Architecture's `.claude/architecture/arch-validate.py` as changed by this slice, and `aac-tools/tests/test_image.py`'s pinned hash (`:20`, checked at `:74-78`) is that file's.

Once the Architecture push has rolled the new service out to production (`https://architecture.webathome.org/api/validate`), `arch-validate` run against production on an artifact holding a number-like string where a string is expected prints the line, the source scalar and the parsed value in the card's form.

ANS-184.2: "Have the generators' YAML writer quote any string that YAML 1.2 would read as a number (`1e5`, `1.5e3`, `0o17`, `089`, `9e10234`)." This holds for both generators that dumped with plain `yaml.safe_dump`: ArgoCDTools `aac-tools/image/gen_architecture.py:1245` and Architecture `tools/ha-fleet/gen-ha-fleet.py:394`. Each such string reads back as the same string through the service's YAML reader.
Both generators write strings that are not number-like, and non-string values, exactly as before. The only change to a generated artifact is the quoting of number-like strings.

items.area: R3 — archive on a failed validate
items.description: ANS-184.3: "If the pipeline change is small, archive the generated architecture file when an AaC validate stage fails." This already holds and needs no pipeline change: every generated architecture file is archived in its Generate stage, before Validate runs. The deploy-repo template archives at JenkinsPipelineUtils `docs/examples/deploy-architecture.groovy:48`, before Validate at `:55`, through `vars/architectureProducer.groovy:52`. FieldnotesDeploy's `Jenkinsfile.architecture` archives at `:47`, before `:54`. IoTSupport's `Jenkinsfile.architecture` archives at `:65`, before `:72`. Architecture's `Jenkinsfile.ha-fleet` archives at `:55`, before `:64`.

items.area: R4 — a wire per container role
items.description: ANS-151: "Wanted: a wire that names its container, or one drawn only on the containers that set the var, so one image with several roles carries a wire per role." This already holds and the slice adds no generator work. An image entry's `containers:` map scopes `upstream` (and `realizes`) to named containers: ArgoCDTools `aac-tools/image/gen_architecture.py:272` and `:950-957`, from commit `14d85ae`, pinned by `tests/test_gen_architecture.py:1319`.

ANS-151: "The same scoping would keep a recipe's `boundByDefaultValue` off containers that never make the call; FieldnotesDeploy's chart now sets `SSE_GATEWAY_URL` on `app` to get that." Under the 2026-10-03 ruling there is no generator scoping. FieldnotesDeploy's chart no longer sets `SSE_GATEWAY_URL` on `app` and no longer carries its comment (`chart/templates/app-deployment.yaml:57-61` at planning). FieldnotesDeploy's prd architecture still generates and validates, and the SSE gateway Serving edge is drawn onto both `app` and `mcp` (the default applies to every instance when no container sets the variable: `gen_architecture.py:1597-1606`).
